claims.quote: Boot-shaped heart CXR Tetralogy of Fallot

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Cardiac: CT ratio <50% on PA (<60% on AP); contour
claims.quote: C - Cardiac: CT ratio <50% on PA (<60% on AP); contour; valves; pacemaker leads.
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Reading Approach (RIPE technical adequacy → ABCDE-FGHI)

claims.text: Chest x-ray: boot-shaped heart with a concave main pulmonary artery segment and diminished pulmonary vascular markings; a right aortic arch is present in 25%
claims.quote: Chest x-ray shows a boot-shaped heart with a concave main pulmonary artery segment and diminished pulmonary vascular markings. A right aortic arch is present in 25%.

claims.text: Causes A large VSD, right ventricular outflow tract and pulmonary valve obstruction, and an over-riding aorta; pulmonary blood flow falls, the RV hypertrophies, and unoxygenated blood enters the aorta via the VSD
claims.quote: Tetralogy of Fallot involves a large ventricular septal defect (VSD), right ventricular outflow tract and pulmonary valve obstruction, and over-riding of the aorta. Pulmonary blood flow is decreased, the right ventricle hypertrophies, and unoxygenated blood enters the aorta via the VSD.

claims.text: Symptoms Depends on the outflow obstruction: severely affected neonates have marked cyanosis, dyspnea with feeding, poor weight gain and a harsh grade 3 to 5/6 systolic ejection murmur (from the pulmonary stenosis; the VSD shunt is silent)
claims.quote: Manifestations depend on the degree of right ventricle outflow obstruction; severely affected neonates have marked cyanosis, dyspnea with feeding, poor weight gain, and a harsh grade 3 to 5/6 systolic ejection murmur. The murmur comes from the pulmonary stenosis; the VSD shunt is silent.

claims.text: Hypercyanotic spells: sudden profound cyanosis and hypoxia that may be triggered by a fall in saturation (crying, defecating), lower systemic vascular resistance (playing, kicking legs), or sudden tachycardia or hypovolemia; the murmur diminishes or disappears during a spell
claims.quote: Hypercyanotic spells are sudden episodes of profound cyanosis and hypoxia that may be triggered by a fall in oxygen saturation (eg, during crying, defecating), decreased systemic vascular resistance (eg, during playing, kicking legs), or sudden tachycardia or hypovolemia. The murmur diminishes or disappears during a spell.

claims.text: Some toddlers squat during play, which raises systemic vascular resistance and arterial oxygen saturation
claims.quote: During play, some toddlers may intermittently squat, a position that increases systemic vascular resistance and aortic pressure, which decreases right-to-left ventricular shunting and thus raises arterial oxygen saturation.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: surgical repair
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Pediatric / Congenital CXR Signs table

claims.text: Neonates with severe cyanosis: prostaglandin E1 infusion to open the ductus arteriosus
claims.quote: Give neonates with severe cyanosis an infusion of prostaglandin E1 to open the ductus arteriosus.

claims.text: Spells: knee-chest position and oxygen; sometimes opioids (morphine or fentanyl), volume expansion, sodium bicarbonate, beta-blockers (propranolol or esmolol) or phenylephrine
claims.quote: Place infants with hypercyanotic spells in the knee-chest position and give oxygen; sometimes, opioids (morphine or fentanyl), volume expansion, sodium bicarbonate, beta-blockers (propranolol or esmolol), or phenylephrine may help.

claims.text: Surgical repair at 2 to 6 months, or earlier if symptoms are severe
claims.quote: Repair surgically at 2 to 6 months or earlier if symptoms are severe.
